sections.h2: Durham County deed counter: location and hours
sections.html:
The deed counter is on the second floor of Durham County Administration Building II, at 201 East Main Street in Durham, NC 27701. It takes filings Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 4:45pm, holidays excluded. The phone number is 919-560-0480.

Plenty of sellers never visit. Their law firm or title agent files the signed deed and receives it back stamped. Since the document itself is what protects you, learn the office's rules before you sign.

Durham County had about 347,240 residents in mid 2025 and 164,222 housing units. Owners occupy 55.5% of homes, and the median owner-occupied value is $389,400. The transfer tax follows price, so a pricier home produces a bigger tax line at closing. Request an itemized estimate from the settlement agent early, and weigh each offer by what you net.

Recording an ordinary deed of 15 pages or fewer is $26.00, with $4 added per extra page. A mortgage is priced on its own line, and a release of one is free of charge.

Recording charges in Durham County
DocumentAmount
Deed or similar paper (not a mortgage)$26.00 for the first 15 pages, then $4 per page
Mortgage or deed of trust$64.00 for the first 35 pages, then $4 per page
Plat map$21.00 for every sheet
Document outside the format rules$25.00 extra
Additional instrument inside one filing$10.00 apiece
Release of a mortgage (satisfaction)No fee
Certified copy of a recorded document$5.00 first page; $2 per page after

Every North Carolina county charges the same scale, set by G.S. 161-10, and you pay at the counter.

The state levies $1 on every $500 of price or value, and a remainder below $500 is treated as a whole unit. Under G.S. 105-228.30 the seller pays it to the register before the deed is filed.

Half the money stays with Durham County's general fund. The other half is remitted to the state each month. You will see the amount on your settlement statement, next to the contract price.

  • The seller carries this cost, so count it when you compare offers.
  • Paying off a deed of trust at closing adds no filing charge for the release.
  • The statute measures the tax on consideration or value, so the deed's stated price matters.

A deed can be recorded over the internet through four approved vendors. A deed that arrives before 4:45 pm is processed and sent back the same business day. An individual who wants an account contacts a vendor directly.

  • Simplifile
  • Indecomm Global Services
  • ePN, the eRecording Partners Network
  • CSC, the Corporation Service Company

Title agents often hold accounts already, which lets a Durham closing finish in one day. If you sign outside a closing, you can bring the original to the counter in person.

sections.h2: Format rules for a printed deed
sections.html:
The Document Recording Standards restate G.S. 161-14(b). A paper that breaks a rule still gets filed once the $25.00 surcharge is paid. Print on white letter or legal paper, one side only, and name the instrument type at the head of page one. Leave three inches of blank room above the text on that first page, keep half inch margins on every other edge, and use type of 9 points or bigger. Plat maps measure 18 by 24, and pen is allowed for blanks and corrections.

When tiny print is the only flaw, the registrar can waive the surcharge if the page is legible.

sections.h2: Why filing protects a seller and buyer
sections.html:
Filing settles who stands first. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed cannot beat a lien creditor or a buyer who gave value until it is registered where the land sits, and between rival papers the earlier registration time prevails.

The office indexes what it is handed and has no power to repair a recorded paper. Misspelled names, defective legal descriptions and wrong parcel numbers are errors outside their power. An indexing slip is reported by email, and the office answers with an Administrative Notice linked to the original entry. Proofread first.

A Recording Notification Service will email you when a document is recorded in your name, which helps guard a vacant house against property fraud.

Property tax is a different office's job. Durham County Tax Administration, 3rd Floor of the same building (919-560-0300), runs it. Real property was last reappraised effective January 1, 2025.

Bills go to whoever owned the parcel on January 1, and one that reaches the wrong person should be handed to the new owner. Before closing, ask the tax collector what is owed so the settlement agent can pay it.

sections.h2: Searching recorded documents before you sell
sections.html:
The county runs an Online Public Records Search, a database of recorded real estate and business documents. Looking up your own parcel before listing shows the deeds, deeds of trust and releases in the chain, so you can confirm an old mortgage shows as released.

That check suits inherited houses and owners who paid off a loan years ago, and a satisfaction is free to file. A certified copy of any recorded paper costs $5.00 for the first page and $2 for each added page.

The office handles more than land records: assumed business names, corporate and partnership certificates, military records, notaries and oaths, plats and vital records such as birth, marriage and death certificates. A marriage license is $60.00 and a certified birth or death copy is $10.00.

sections.h2: Closing steps and a cash sale
sections.html:
On a typical sale, the settlement agent prepares the deed, you sign it, and the agent files it at the counter or electronically with the transfer tax and fee. Check that the first page names the instrument and that every name is spelled correctly, since the office cannot fix errors later.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, but the deed, the transfer tax and the recording fee are still due. Ask for the stamped, recorded deed back and keep it with your closing papers.

If you are paying off a mortgage at closing, the lender records a release, and the filing costs nothing. Later, search your own parcel online to confirm the release appears. It is worth doing a few weeks after closing, since a missing release can surface when the buyer sells or refinances. Staff at 919-560-0480 can tell you whether a document has been received.

faqs.q: Who pays the Durham County excise tax at a sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays, handing it to the register of deeds before filing. The rate is $1 per $500 of price, counting any leftover fraction. Durham County keeps half and the state receives half.

faqs.q: Does Durham County charge to file a mortgage payoff?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule shows no fee for a satisfaction, so releasing a deed of trust at closing costs nothing at the register of deeds.

faqs.q: What if my deed is printed in tiny type?
faqs.a: The office can still file it. Missing a layout rule triggers a $25.00 nonstandard surcharge, though the registrar may skip it when the only flaw is print under 9 points and the page reads clearly.

faqs.q: Can a homeowner e-record a deed alone in Durham County?
faqs.a: Usually through a vendor. The county names Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, ePN and CSC, and each sets up its own account. A submission received by 4:45 pm comes back the same business day.

faqs.q: How do I correct a misspelled name on a Durham County deed?
faqs.a: Staff cannot change it, because documents are recorded and indexed as presented. Your closing attorney can advise how to correct the deed. Email the office only about an indexing error, and it replies with an Administrative Notice.
